name: oc-time-report
description: Estimation-vs-logged-hours report over a period (independent of the AI-usage JSON). Tempo-worklog driven and TICKET-based with PER-AREA columns. Tickets are selected by their DATE (resolutiondate, else updated) in the window, and every worklog on a selected ticket counts (all-time, so per-ticket totals match Jira's aggregatetimespent). One row per ticket with a column group for each area (Backend/Frontend/QA) giving that area's main developer, Architect & Dev-lead estimates, total dev / logged / sub-bug hours each split into AI and non-AI streams (a worklog is AI-assisted when its author holds an AI-metrics record covering that issue — a US's record also covers its non-bug sub-tasks, since US dev work is booked on sub-tasks, while a sub-bug uses its own record; no more per-area AI flag), two time gains (Architect and Dev-lead, each with/without sub-bugs; every aggregate gain — Totals-by-area, per month, and the Arch-gain-by-month table — is computed over only the tickets carrying that estimate, so an unestimated ticket's logged hours never inflate it, while the Est/Logged columns still show full sums) and a sub-bug count; a single Arch-gain B/F/Q column (considering bugs) and a Logged+bug B/F/Q/OH column right after the Final flag; a Total logged d column (the ticket's full logged time — all areas' logged + all sub-bug + overhead — equal to Jira's aggregate logged time when every worklog author is on the roster) and an Overall arch gain column (accumulated Arch estimate vs total dev, incl. overhead, as a gain) placed right before the Backend section; and closing Overhead d / Overhead % / Overhead people columns. Overhead people (Architect/PO/DevOps/Consultant/management, roster area 'overhead') never count as an area developer — their hours go to the Overhead bucket, itemised per person with hours. Each area's main developer is its top contributor by dev-logged + own sub-bug-fixing hours (a token reviewer never wins). Every ticket carries a Date (resolutiondate, else updated) and is grouped by month; the HTML splits into five tabs (All, User Stories All, User Stories Final, Bugs Final, Bugs and Others), each with Totals-by-area overall + per month and the per-ticket matrix grouped by month. Per-ticket rows also carry a Fix ver column (the Jira Fix Version/s, all shown) right after Type. Totals-by-area (shown in days, 1 d = 8 h) is one row per area with a Project column, % (right after Total dev d; share of total logged), % AI (right after it; all AI-assisted hours / the area's total dev = (Log AI + Sub-bug AI) / (Logged + Sub-bug)), Log AI d / Log non d (the logged AI/non-AI split), SB AI d / SB non d (the sub-bug AI/non-AI split), % Sub-bug (sub-bug share of the area), and a single with-bug Arch gain and DL gain (each with ticket count). The HTML has two live picklists — Project and Fix version — that recompute the Totals, the by-month tables and their ticket counts (hiding months with no match) and filter the per-ticket rows. Fix version is grouped by release line (e.g. 17.x, 17.2.x): selecting a group matches every ticket whose version equals or starts with that base, while the per-ticket Fix ver column still shows each ticket's complete version number. Right after the Totals-by-area table the HTML shows an Arch-gain-by-month summary (rows = months; columns Overall gain/Backend/Frontend/QA/Overhead; Overall gain = (total Arch estimate - total dev)/total Arch estimate for the month, i.e. total dev/total Arch est as a gain over every ticket; each area cell = Architect gain with sub-bugs + ticket count and AI share of dev hours in parentheses; the Overhead column instead shows overhead's share of that month's total logged hours). Tempo is fetched with a persistent month-bucketed cache (only the recent ~45 days re-fetched each run). Also writes a second finished-User-Story per-developer summary (per area main dev, split by AI true/false, grouped by month). The roster is embedded (accountId -> name/area/role/active). HTML + CSV to ./docs/, named with the run date and the window start and end (time-report-<date>-<start>-<end>.{html,csv}). Jira via direct REST and Tempo per-user, both mandatory tokens; no Atlassian MCP.
